cause: after the question was approved and ideas 1-6 filed

1-time-each-step-of-the-import-duplicate.line: The baseline every other idea is judged against, and it says which step is worth attacking.

why.impact: Without per-step times none of the speed-ups can be judged.
why.odds: Timing a fixed import is straightforward and almost certain to produce a table.
why.path: Ideas 2 to 6 all wait for its numbers.

4-compute-the-full-file-hash-only-when-a.line: Skips a whole read of every new file, which is most of a typical import, with a small change.

why.impact: Removes one of the roughly three full reads per new file.
why.odds: Most incoming files have no sampled-hash match, so the saving is almost guaranteed to show.
why.path: Changes what idea 2 can still save, so it goes before it.

2-read-each-incoming-file-once-for-the-s.line: Folds the remaining repeat reads into one, but much of its saving overlaps idea 4.

why.impact: Worth most on large files and cold disks.
why.odds: A warm page cache may make the repeat reads nearly free.
why.path: Best judged after idea 4 shows what reads are left.

5-store-each-picture-s-full-file-hash-so.line: Big win for re-importing folders already in the library, but it needs a migration and a staleness guard.

why.impact: Halves the reads for every duplicate file.
why.odds: The design was rejected once for the scan, and keeping a stored hash honest when a file changes is the hard part.

3-look-up-all-of-a-batch-s-files-in-one-.line: Only matters if the timing shows the per-file writer round trips are slow.

why.impact: Large only when the writer thread is busy with background work.
why.odds: A single indexed lookup is usually under a millisecond, so it may be negligible.

6-hash-the-staged-import-s-files-in-para.line: Overlaps idea 4 and depends on the disk, so it comes last.

why.impact: Shrinks hashing time only, which ideas 4 and 2 already cut.
why.odds: Helps on SSDs and may hurt on a spinning disk.
